events.title: Kant is born
events.text: Immanuel Kant is born on 22 April in the Sattlergasse, the fourth child of a harness-maker.

events.title: One city
events.text: On 13 June the king unites the Altstadt, Löbenicht and Kneiphof into the single city of Königsberg.

events.title: Pietist school
events.text: Kant enters the strict Pietist Collegium Fridericianum, where he stays until 1740.

events.title: Euler's bridges
events.text: Leonhard Euler proves that no walk can cross each of the city's seven bridges exactly once.

events.title: The Albertina
events.text: At sixteen Kant enrols at the university, beside the cathedral on the Kneiphof.

events.title: Father dies
events.text: Kant's father dies; Kant soon leaves to earn a living as a family tutor.

events.title: Magister Kant
events.text: Kant takes his degree and begins teaching, paid by his students; his book on the heavens proposes that the solar system formed from a cloud of matter.

events.title: Russians arrive
events.text: In January Russian troops occupy the city; Kant, like everyone, swears allegiance to Empress Elizabeth.

events.title: A plea to the empress
events.text: Kant applies to Elizabeth for the chair of logic; it goes to another man.

events.title: Russians leave
events.text: The Russian occupation ends as Russia makes peace with Prussia.

events.title: Magistergasse
events.text: In the early 1760s Kant lodges in the Magistergasse on the Kneiphof, until ships and carts drive him out.

events.title: Castle librarian
events.text: Kant becomes sub-librarian of the royal castle library, his first salary.

events.title: At Kanter's
events.text: Kant lodges with the bookseller Kanter in the Löbenicht, until a neighbour's rooster drives him out.

events.title: Professor
events.text: Kant becomes professor of logic and metaphysics, aged forty-six.

events.title: Ochsenmarkt
events.text: Kant moves to lodgings on the Ochsenmarkt, east of the Kneiphof.

events.title: Critique of Pure Reason
events.text: After a decade of near silence, Kant publishes the Critique of Pure Reason.

events.title: His own house
events.text: Kant moves into his own house on the Prinzessinstraße, near the castle, with a lecture room downstairs.

events.title: What is Enlightenment?
events.text: 'Sapere aude! Have courage to use your own understanding!'

events.title: Groundwork
events.text: The Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals sets out the categorical imperative.

events.title: Rector
events.text: Kant serves as rector of the university, again in 1788.

events.title: Royal rebuke
events.text: The king's government forbids Kant to write on religion; he promises, as the king's subject.

events.title: Perpetual Peace
events.text: Kant publishes Toward Perpetual Peace, a plan for a federation of free states.

events.title: 'It is good'
events.text: Kant dies at home on 12 February; his reported last words are 'Es ist gut'.

events.title: Burial
events.text: Kant is buried in the professors' vault of the cathedral.

events.title: New university
events.text: The Albertina moves to a new building on the Paradeplatz.

events.title: Kant statue
events.text: Christian Daniel Rauch's bronze statue of Kant is unveiled.

events.title: House demolished
events.text: Kant's house on the Prinzessinstraße is torn down.

events.title: The starry heavens
events.text: A plaque on the castle wall quotes Kant: the starry heavens above me and the moral law within me.

events.title: Kant's tomb
events.text: For his 200th birthday a new open pillared hall is built over Kant's tomb.

events.title: RAF raids
events.text: On two nights in August, RAF bombers burn the old city; some 4,200 to 5,000 people die.

events.title: Siege
events.text: The Red Army storms Königsberg on 6–9 April; General Lasch surrenders.

events.title: Kaliningrad
events.text: On 4 July the city is renamed Kaliningrad, after the Soviet leader Mikhail Kalinin.

events.title: Deportations
events.text: From 1947 to 1948 about one hundred thousand remaining Germans are deported to Germany.

events.title: Castle blown up
events.text: The castle ruins are dynamited; a House of Soviets later rises on the site, never finished.

events.title: Statue returns
events.text: A recast of Rauch's Kant statue, funded on Marion Dönhoff's initiative, is set up at the university.

events.title: Cathedral rebuilt
events.text: The cathedral, a shell since 1944, is rebuilt with German help beside Kant's tomb.

events.title: Kant University
events.text: The university is renamed after Immanuel Kant for the city's 750th anniversary.

events.title: Pink paint
events.text: During a contest to name the airport, Kant's tomb and statue are splashed with paint and he is called a traitor.

events.title: Kant at 300
events.text: Kant's tercentenary is marked in Kaliningrad and in Germany, amid the war in Ukraine.

events.title: House of Soviets gone
events.text: The unfinished House of Soviets on the castle site is demolished.

chartNote: Share of the area inside the city wall of 1626–34, by quarter. Quarters follow the city plan of 1763 and their boundaries are approximate; rivers follow today's courses. A colour stands for a whole quarter, though Kant's house, school and route were single streets, and the route of his walk is a reconstruction.
